title: Sunnybrook Church prepares annual cookie dough fundraiser - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero Maren Ewertz No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — For more than 30 years, Sunnybrook Community Church has held its annual cookie dough fundraiser to support the church’s mission trips.
“[It’s] a church recipe that only a few people know,” said Sunnybrook’s High School Ministry Director Carter Prescott.
More than 200 people gathered inside the church’s Hope Center to combine the 869 pounds of chocolate, 965 pounds of flour, 430 pounds of sugar, 386 pounds of butter, and 772 eggs.
The day started with prepackaging, then as students got out of school, the work really picked up. Balling the dough, flash-freezing it, then packing for sale.
Story continues below
Kids at Sunnybrook, like Sophie Benz and Lydia White, explained their roles in the process.
“Making cookie dough and rolling it into balls,” said Benz.
“Making cookie dough for the fundraiser,” said White.
Sunnybrook kids plan to sell the dough to friends, family, and church members.
“We’re raising over $25,000 for students to go on these trips. Which is incredible,” said Prescott. “For every dozen that a student sells, they get to keep 80% of the proceeds.”
Benz and White told KCAU 9 why they were going on a mission trip.
“To learn about Jesus and strengthen my faith,” said Benz.
“To grow my faith and hang out with friends,” said White.
Youth nights at Sunnybrook Community Church are on Wednesday night
